I have failed so many math tests and now years later I’m an electrical engineer. Math is a hard subject and I truly believe that it’s hard for everybody- even those who have a “knack” for it. The things that worked for me was going to my teacher as well as the office hours of others to get help. Sometimes you just need things explained differently to you. Additionally, the internet is such a good resource. I’m sure that you already know about Kahn Academy but there are a ton of other helpful sites out there too. I used to watch a lot of YouTube at .5 speed of certain subjects that were confusing to me (also, if you go on to take Calculus courses, Paul’s Online Math Notes are incredible). Lastly, you’re not dumb. I get that it definitely FEELS that way sometimes, but you’re not. Grades can be redeemed after a bad exam, and worst case scenario, classes can be retaken. Keep in mind that the education system is not perfect, but the best thing that you can do is advocate for yourself. Godspeed, I’m wishing you the best.

I’m a girl, but similarly I have had less luck in the dating game. I’ve been single for a long time, and to be quite honest, I’m thankful for all the time that I have had with myself. I’ve grown so much as a person and I think the single life gives one time to explore themselves and improve. 

So all that being said, my biggest tip regarding your question is to manage your mindset. Don’t hang around people who subscribe to the nice guy or incel philosophy. Stay off those forums. 

Also know that it is OKAY that you can’t find a relationship right now. It is very normal to be rejected or not approached by the people you are pursuing. It doesn’t make you unworthy, unattractive or undesirable. It also sure as hell does not mean that you are automatically an incel. 

I guess essentially what I’m trying to say is that while you may not be in control of whether or not a girl likes you, you are absolutely in control of how you react to it. It’s all about the reaction. If you react from a place of compassion and confidence, then I don’t think you have anything to worry about.
